19-player-publish/shared-library/items/c.title: Crystal of Naphkon
19-player-publish/shared-library/items/c.description: Type: Item Category: item Chapter: Chapter 1To fashion a crystal of Naphkon requires a large amethyst, which can be easily purchased in New York City for $20 for a rough, poor quality stone. Higher quality stones cost $50 to $100+.See Create Crystal of Naphkon, page 161.Once created, the crystal may be used to home in on the kidnapped psyches.A character may activate the crystal with either: A successful Clairvoyance roll and 1D6+1 magic points, or A successful Psychometry roll and 1D6+1 magic points if touching a possession of one of the victims, such as bedding or an empty bottle from the cellar. Without psychic talents, activation requires: A successful Hard POW roll, and 1D8+5 magic points. The process is similar to viewing different times and places, but the costs and process are slightly different due to the psychic turmoil caused by this event.The vision reveals six men and women trapped in an unfurnished room with marble floors and walls. All of them are wearing amethyst necklaces. They are dressed in loose tunics, and the men have forked beards.One is frantically pounding on the door, while others pace or slump dejectedly. There is one tall, thin window, too narrow to squeeze through.Suddenly, all of the inhabitants react, apparently to sounds outside. One of them runs to the window and looks down. The viewer now sees that they are in a high tower.Down below, flames are spreading through a partly ruined city, and tunic-clad, gray-eyed people are fighting shaggy umber-colored humanoids. A six-legged, white-furred beast with a horn jutting from its head rampages past.The vision ends abruptly with a sense of impending doom for the victims.The experience costs the viewer 0/1D4 Sanity points.Heroes who wish to rescue Brendan Sterling and the others need to figure out how to get to them and gather their psyches. See Chapter 6 for details on how this rescue can be accomplished.The heroes can attempt this rescue practically any time, though it is best accomplished before tracking down the Lomarian-possessed bodies.Having experienced the vision of Sterling and the others, a hero may attempt a Cthulhu Mythos roll to deduce their location in ancient Lomar.Alternatively, heroes using the details from the vision may conduct research in any Mythos tomes they encounter or possess to fathom the victims' location. Use the tome in question's Mythos Rating to determine if the heroes find matching information concerning: Gray-eyed peoples: Lomarians Shaggy umber-colored humanoids: Voormi Six-legged furred beasts: Gnoph-kehs Together, these details place Brendan Sterling and the others in forgotten Lomar, some 25,000 years in the past.See Call of Cthulhu Rulebook, page 175 for Mythos tome ratings.Back to Shared Items

19-player-publish/shared-library/items/h.title: Heart of Dreams
19-player-publish/shared-library/items/h.description: Type: Item Category: dreamlands-artifactHearts of Dreams are rare items, much sought after by those who know and understand their abilities. The hearts are known by different names; many have cultural associations or are related to the land of dream, and much myth and folklore surround them.One legend concerning the hearts seems to cross cultural boundaries and concerns the foul keepers or guardians of the hearts, who torment those who risk using a heart’s power without due deference to Hypnos, Lord of Dream.These strange devices usually take the form of a red crystalline cube run through with jagged lines of yellow material.A Heart of Dreams is used to view other places in dream. These places could include distant lands, planets, and other dimensions.In addition, a heart can enable its user to physically bring items or living things back with them from the Dreamlands, provided such things are held by the dreamer.Using a Heart of Dreams requires a successful Cthulhu Mythos roll.In addition, a successful Luck roll determines whether the heart’s keeper detects the item’s use.The Luck roll may be ignored if an Extreme success is achieved with the Cthulhu Mythos roll, indicating that the user did not displease Hypnos, the prime creator and owner of the hearts.Back to Shared Items

19-player-publish/shared-rules/skills/cl.title: Clairvoyance
19-player-publish/shared-rules/skills/cl.description: Category: skillsPsychic perception beyond normal senses; readings about objects, people, locations, events, ghosts, or invisible presences.Also known as second sight, clairvoyance enables perception beyond the normal human senses, allowing the psychic to gain information about an object, person, location, or physical event. The clairvoyant may sense ghosts and invisible Mythos creatures, identify the rough whereabouts of a missing object or person, detect whether a tragic event occurred in a certain place, and so on. The psychic concentrates for 1D6 rounds, focusing solely on the thing they wish to know about, spending 1D6+1 magic points in the process, and making a Clairvoyance roll. If the roll fails, the psychic is unable to determine anything and may attempt to push the roll (requiring a further spend of 5 magic points). A success means the psychic is able to perceive some relevant information. The nature and detail of the information gained are the purview of the Keeper. Often such information will be vague or incomplete. If an outside force (another psychic, monster, etc.) does not wish to be “read” then the difficulty level of the roll is raised. Certain objects may assist in a reading, such a photograph of a missing person or an object personal to the clairvoyant hero. In such situations, the Keeper may reduce the difficulty of the skill roll. If the psychic reads and senses a Mythos presence, or somehow connects with the alien intelligence, they must make a Sanity roll, losing the usual amount for that monster. Other situations may also call for Sanity rolls at the Keeper's discretion. Psychic Skills - Access and Limits Psychic Attack Psychic Attacks and Possession Back to Skills Rules

19-player-publish/shared-rules/skills/ct.title: Cthulhu Mythos
19-player-publish/shared-rules/skills/ct.description: Category: skillsPlayer states an aim; Keeper may suggest a weaker one. Default difficulty = Regular (roll ≤ Cthulhu Mythos). When affecting a resisting target, treat as an opposed roll Cthulhu Mythos vs POW.Physical harm: Spend MP, lose half that amount of SAN; on a successful opposed roll the target takes damage equal to MP spent (horrific effects). Banish monster: Pay MP = ⅕ × monster POW + 1D4 SAN; succeed on opposed roll to banish. Communion with the dead: Recent dead - 10 MP + 1D10 SAN, lasts 1D6 rounds. Long‑term dead - 15 MP + 1D10 SAN, lasts 1D4 rounds. Physical ward: Variable MP/SAN; each MP adds one point of armor (no protection vs. mental/psychic attacks). Understand Mythos languages: 8 MP + 1D6 SAN; comprehension lasts ~1 hour.Back to Skills Rules

info_showOrphanNodes.description: Show nodes that are not connected to any other nodes.

info_showAttachments.description: Show attachments like images and PDFs as nodes in the graph.

info_allowGlobalGraph.description: Allow the user to view the global graph of all nodes.

info_allowExpand.description: Allow the user to pop-out the graph view to take up the whole screen

info_attractionForce.description: How much should linked nodes attract each other? This will make the graph appear more clustered.

info_linkLength.description: How long should the links between nodes be? The shorter the links the more connected nodes will cluster together.

info_repulsionForce.description: How much should nodes repel each other? This will make disconnected parts more spread out.

info_centralForce.description: How much should nodes be attracted to the center? This will make the graph appear more dense and circular.

info_edgePruning.description: Edges with a length above this threshold will not be rendered, however they will still contribute to the simulation. This can help large tangled graphs look more organised. Hovering over a node will still display these links.

info_minNodeRadius.description: How small should the smallest nodes be? The smaller a node is the less it will attract other nodes.

info_maxNodeRadius.description: How large should the largest nodes be? Nodes are sized by how many links they have. The larger a node is the more it will attract other nodes. This can be used to create a good grouping around the most important nodes.
